# /graphify

Turn any folder of files into a navigable knowledge graph with community detection, an honest audit trail, and three outputs: interactive HTML, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a plain-language GRAPH_REPORT.md.

## Usage

```
/graphify                                             # full pipeline on current directory (HTML viz; add --obsidian for a vault)
/graphify <path>                                      # full pipeline on specific path
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>           # clone repo then run full pipeline on it
/graphify https://github.com/<owner>/<repo> --branch <branch>  # clone a specific branch
/graphify <url1> <url2> ...                           # clone multiple repos, build each, merge into one cross-repo graph
/graphify <path> --mode deep                          # thorough extraction, richer INFERRED edges
/graphify <path> --update                             # incremental - re-extract only new/changed files
/graphify <path> --directed                            # build directed graph (preserves edge direction: source→target)
/graphify <path> --whisper-model medium                # use a larger Whisper model for better transcription accuracy
/graphify <path> --cluster-only                       # rerun clustering on existing graph
/graphify <path> --no-viz                             # skip visualization, just report + JSON
/graphify <path> --html                               # (HTML is generated by default - this flag is a no-op)
/graphify <path> --svg                                # also export graph.svg (embeds in Notion, GitHub)
/graphify <path> --graphml                            # export graph.graphml (Gephi, yEd)
/graphify <path> --neo4j                              # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for Neo4j
/graphify <path> --neo4j-push bolt://localhost:7687   # push directly to Neo4j
/graphify <path> --falkordb                           # generate graphify-out/cypher.txt for FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --falkordb-push falkordb://localhost:6379   # push directly to FalkorDB
/graphify <path> --mcp                                # start MCP stdio server for agent access
/graphify <path> --watch                              # watch folder, auto-rebuild on code changes (no LLM needed)
/graphify <path> --wiki                               # build agent-crawlable wiki (index.md + one article per community)
/graphify <path> --obsidian --obsidian-dir ~/vaults/my-project  # write vault to custom path (e.g. existing vault)
/graphify add <url>                                   # fetch URL, save to ./raw, update graph
/graphify add <url> --author "Name"                   # tag who wrote it
/graphify add <url> --contributor "Name"              # tag who added it to the corpus
/graphify query "<question>"                          # BFS traversal - broad context
/graphify query "<question>" --dfs                    # DFS - trace a specific path
/graphify query "<question>" --budget 1500            # cap answer at N tokens
/graphify path "AuthModule" "Database"                # shortest path between two concepts
/graphify explain "SwinTransformer"                   # plain-language explanation of a node
```

## What graphify is for

Drop any folder of code, docs, papers, images, or video into graphify and get a queryable knowledge graph. Persistent across sessions, honest audit trail (EXTRACTED/INFERRED/AMBIGUOUS), community detection surfaces cross-document connections you wouldn't think to ask about.

## What You Must Do When Invoked

If the user invoked `/graphify --help` or `/graphify -h` (with no other arguments), print the contents of the `## Usage` section above verbatim and stop. Do not run any commands, do not detect files, do not default the path to `.`. Just print the Usage block and return.

**Fast path — existing graph:** Before doing anything else, check whether `graphify-out/graph.json` exists. The expected location is `graphify-out/graph.json` relative to the **current working directory** (i.e. the project root where you are running commands). If it exists AND the user's request is a natural-language question about the codebase (e.g. "How does X work?", "What calls Y?", "Trace the data flow through Z") and NOT an explicit rebuild command (`--update`, `--cluster-only`, or a bare path/URL that implies fresh extraction): **skip Steps 1–5 entirely and jump straight to `## For /graphify query`.** Run `graphify query "<question>"` immediately. Do not run detect. Do not check corpus size. Do not ask the user to narrow. The graph is already built — use it.

Only when the path is one or more `https://github.com/...` URLs, or several local subfolders to merge. See `references/github-and-merge.md` for the clone, cross-repo merge, and monorepo flow, then continue with the resolved local path. A plain local path skips this step.

```bash
# Detect the correct Python interpreter (handles uv tool, pipx, venv, system installs)
PYTHON=""
GRAPHIFY_BIN=$(which graphify 2>/dev/null)
# 1. uv tool installs — most reliable on modern Mac/Linux
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    _UV_PY=$(uv tool run graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
    if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
fi
# 2. Read shebang from graphify binary (pipx and direct pip installs)
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ] && [ -n "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" ]; then
    _SHEBANG=$(head -1 "$GRAPHIFY_BIN" | tr -d '#!')
    case "$_SHEBANG" in
        *[!a-zA-Z0-9/_.@-]*) ;;
        *) "$_SHEBANG" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null && PYTHON="$_SHEBANG" ;;
    esac
fi
# 3. Fall back to python3
if [ -z "$PYTHON" ]; then PYTHON="python3"; fi
if ! "$PYTHON" -c "import graphify" 2>/dev/null; then
    if command -v uv >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        uv tool install --upgrade graphifyy -q 2>&1 | tail -3
        _UV_PY=$(uv tool run graphifyy python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)" 2>/dev/null)
        if [ -n "$_UV_PY" ]; then PYTHON="$_UV_PY"; fi
    else
        "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q 2>/dev/null \
          || "$PYTHON" -m pip install graphifyy -q --break-system-packages 2>&1 | tail -3
    fi
fi
# Write interpreter path for all subsequent steps (persists across invocations)
mkdir -p graphify-out
"$PYTHON" -c "import sys; open('graphify-out/.graphify_python', 'w', encoding='utf-8').write(sys.executable)"
# Save scan root so `graphify update` (no args) knows where to look next time
echo "$(cd INPUT_PATH && pwd)" > graphify-out/.graphify_root
```

**In every subsequent bash block, replace `python3` with `$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python)` to use the correct interpreter.**

### Step 2 - Detect files

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "

from graphify.detect import detect
from pathlib import Path
result = detect(Path('INPUT_PATH'))

  docs:     N files (.md .txt ...)

  images:   N files
  video:    N files (.mp4 .mp3 ...)

Omit any category with 0 files from the summary.

Then act on it:
- If `total_files` is 0: stop with "No supported files found in [path]."

- If `total_words` > 2,000,000 OR `total_files` > 500: show the warning. Then compute the top 5 first-level subdirectories by file count:
  - Read `scan_root` from the detect JSON (always an absolute path to the resolved INPUT_PATH).

  - Filter out any path that starts with `scan_root + "/graphify-out/"` to exclude converted sidecars.

            if 3 <= len(t) <= 30:
                vocab.add(t)

```

   - You MUST pick only tokens present in the vocabulary file. Do NOT invent tokens.
   - If a query concept has no plausible token in the vocab, skip it — do not substitute a near-synonym from training memory.
   - If **no** vocab tokens match the query at all, output an empty list and tell the user the corpus has no relevant vocabulary for this question. Do not fabricate a search.
   - Translate cross-language: Russian "аутентификация" → look for `auth`, `credential`, `token`, `security` IFF present in vocab.
   - Morphology: "handlers" maps to `handler` IFF present; "todos" maps to `todo` IFF present.

3. Print the selection explicitly to the user before running the query, so the expansion is auditable:
```
Query expanded to (from graph vocab, N tokens): [token1, token2, ...]
```
If the list is empty, say so plainly and stop — do not proceed to traversal.

### Step 1 — Traversal

Build the **expanded query string** by joining the selected tokens with spaces. Use this string as `QUESTION` below — NOT the original user question. (The original question is preserved only for `save-result` at the end.)

Prefer the CLI when it is installed:
```bash
graphify query "QUESTION"
# or: graphify query "QUESTION" --dfs --budget 3000
```

If the CLI is unavailable, load `graphify-out/graph.json` and run the traversal inline:

1. Find the 1-3 nodes whose label best matches the expanded tokens.
2. Run the appropriate traversal from each starting node.
3. Read the subgraph - node labels, edge relations, confidence tags, source locations.
4. Answer using **only** what the graph contains. Quote `source_location` when citing a specific fact.
5. If the graph lacks enough information, say so - do not hallucinate edges.

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "
import sys, json
from networkx.readwrite import json_graph
import networkx as nx
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/graph.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
G = json_graph.node_link_graph(data, edges='links')

question = 'QUESTION'
mode = 'MODE'  # 'bfs' or 'dfs'
terms = [t.lower() for t in question.split() if len(t) >= 3]  # match the vocab threshold; keeps api/jwt/ios (#1392)

# Find best-matching start nodes
scored = []
for nid, ndata in G.nodes(data=True):
    label = ndata.get('label', '').lower()
    score = sum(1 for t in terms if t in label)
    if score > 0:
        scored.append((score, nid))
scored.sort(reverse=True)
start_nodes = [nid for _, nid in scored[:3]]

if not start_nodes:
    print('No matching nodes found for query terms:', terms)
    sys.exit(0)

subgraph_nodes = set()
subgraph_edges = []

if mode == 'dfs':
    # DFS: follow one path as deep as possible before backtracking.
    # Depth-limited to 6 to avoid traversing the whole graph.
    visited = set()
    stack = [(n, 0) for n in reversed(start_nodes)]
    while stack:
        node, depth = stack.pop()
        if node in visited or depth > 6:
            continue
        visited.add(node)
        subgraph_nodes.add(node)
        for neighbor in G.neighbors(node):
            if neighbor not in visited:
                stack.append((neighbor, depth + 1))
                subgraph_edges.append((node, neighbor))
else:
    # BFS: explore all neighbors layer by layer up to depth 3.
    frontier = set(start_nodes)
    subgraph_nodes = set(start_nodes)
    for _ in range(3):
        next_frontier = set()
        for n in frontier:
            for neighbor in G.neighbors(n):
                if neighbor not in subgraph_nodes:
                    next_frontier.add(neighbor)
                    subgraph_edges.append((n, neighbor))
        subgraph_nodes.update(next_frontier)
        frontier = next_frontier

# Token-budget aware output: rank by relevance, cut at budget (~4 chars/token)
token_budget = BUDGET  # default 2000
char_budget = token_budget * 4

# Score each node by term overlap for ranked output
def relevance(nid):
    label = G.nodes[nid].get('label', '').lower()
    return sum(1 for t in terms if t in label)

ranked_nodes = sorted(subgraph_nodes, key=relevance, reverse=True)

lines = [f'Traversal: {mode.upper()} | Start: {[G.nodes[n].get(\"label\",n) for n in start_nodes]} | {len(subgraph_nodes)} nodes']
for nid in ranked_nodes:
    d = G.nodes[nid]
    lines.append(f'  NODE {d.get(\"label\", nid)} [src={d.get(\"source_file\",\"\")} loc={d.get(\"source_location\",\"\")}]')
for u, v in subgraph_edges:
    if u in subgraph_nodes and v in subgraph_nodes:
        _raw = G[u][v]; d = next(iter(_raw.values()), {}) if isinstance(G, nx.MultiGraph) else _raw
        lines.append(f'  EDGE {G.nodes[u].get(\"label\",u)} --{d.get(\"relation\",\"\")} [{d.get(\"confidence\",\"\")}]--> {G.nodes[v].get(\"label\",v)}')

output = '\n'.join(lines)
if len(output) > char_budget:
    output = output[:char_budget] + f'\n... (truncated at ~{token_budget} token budget - use --budget N for more)'
print(output)
"
```

Replace `QUESTION` with the **expanded** query string, `MODE` with `bfs` or `dfs`, and `BUDGET` with the token budget (default `2000`, or whatever `--budget N` specifies). Then answer based on the subgraph output above, using only what the graph contains.

After writing the answer, save it back into the graph so it improves future queries. Include the expanded tokens inside the `--answer` text (e.g. `"Expanded from original query via vocab: [tokens]. Then traversed..."`) so the next `--update` extracts the expansion history as a graph node:

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -m graphify save-result --question "ORIGINAL_QUESTION" --answer "ANSWER" --type query --nodes NODE1 NODE2
```

Replace `ORIGINAL_QUESTION` with the user's verbatim question, `ANSWER` with your full answer text (containing the expanded-token trace), `NODE1 NODE2` with the list of node labels you cited. This closes the feedback loop: the next `--update` will extract this Q&A as a node in the graph.

**Work memory (self-improving loop).** Add an `--outcome` so future sessions learn from this one — append `--outcome useful|dead_end|corrected` to the `save-result` command (and `--correction "the right answer"` when correcting):

- `useful` — the cited nodes answered the question well (they become *preferred sources*).
- `dead_end` — the question/path led nowhere; don't re-derive it next time.
- `corrected` — the saved answer was wrong; `--correction` records what was right.

At the **start** of graph work, refresh and read the lessons: run `graphify reflect --if-stale` (cheap, deterministic, no LLM; `--if-stale` makes it a no-op when `LESSONS.md` is already newer than every input, e.g. when the git hook just refreshed it), then read `graphify-out/reflections/LESSONS.md`. It lists **preferred sources** (start there), **known dead ends** (skip them), and prior **corrections**. Running `reflect` yourself keeps the lessons current even without the git hook installed; if the post-commit hook *is* installed, `--if-stale` means your session-start run costs almost nothing.

---

## For /graphify path

Find the shortest path between two named concepts in the graph. Prefer the CLI when installed:

```bash
graphify path "NODE_A" "NODE_B"
```

If the CLI is unavailable, run it inline:

```bash
$(cat graphify-out/.graphify_python) -c "

import networkx as nx
from networkx.readwrite import json_graph
from pathlib import Path

data = json.loads(Path('graphify-out/graph.json').read_text(encoding='utf-8'))
G = json_graph.node_link_graph(data, edges='links')

a_term = 'NODE_A'
b_term = 'NODE_B'

def find_node(term):
    term = term.lower()
    scored = sorted(
        [(sum(1 for w in term.split() if w in G.nodes[n].get('label','').lower()), n)
         for n in G.nodes()],
        reverse=True
    )
    return scored[0][1] if scored and scored[0][0] > 0 else None

src = find_node(a_term)
tgt = find_node(b_term)

if not src or not tgt:
    print(f'Could not find nodes matching: {a_term!r} or {b_term!r}')
    sys.exit(0)

try:
    path = nx.shortest_path(G, src, tgt)
    print(f'Shortest path ({len(path)-1} hops):')
    for i, nid in enumerate(path):
        label = G.nodes[nid].get('label', nid)
        if i < len(path) - 1:
            _raw = G[nid][path[i+1]]; edge = next(iter(_raw.values()), {}) if isinstance(G, nx.MultiGraph) else _raw
            rel = edge.get('relation', '')
            conf = edge.get('confidence', '')
            print(f'  {label} --{rel}--> [{conf}]')
        else:
            print(f'  {label}')
except nx.NetworkXNoPath:
    print(f'No path found between {a_term!r} and {b_term!r}')
except nx.NodeNotFound as e:
    print(f'Node not found: {e}')
"
```

def text(node) -> str:
    return "".join(node.itertext()).strip() if node is not None else ""


def pub_date(article) -> str | None:
    for path in [".//ArticleDate", ".//JournalIssue/PubDate"]:
        node = article.find(path)
        if node is not None:
            year = node.findtext("Year")
            if not year:
                m = re.search(r"\b(19|20)\d{2}\b", node.findtext("MedlineDate", ""))
                if m:
                    return m.group(0)
                continue
            month = node.findtext("Month")
            day = node.findtext("Day")
            if month and month.isdigit():
                return f"{year}-{int(month):02d}" + (f"-{int(day):02d}" if day and day.isdigit() else "")
            return year
    return None


def parse_pubmed(xml: str, retrieved_at: str) -> list[SourceDocument]:
    root = ET.fromstring(xml)
    docs = []
    for item in root.findall(".//PubmedArticle"):
        pmid = item.findtext("./MedlineCitation/PMID", "")
        if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{1,10}", pmid):
            continue
        title = text(item.find(".//ArticleTitle"))
        abstract = [
            {"label": n.get("Label", "Abstract"), "text": text(n)}
            for n in item.findall(".//Abstract/AbstractText")
            if text(n)
        ]
        ids = {n.get("IdType"): text(n) for n in item.findall(".//ArticleId")}
        types = [text(n) for n in item.findall(".//PublicationType")]
        comments = [n.get("RefType", "") for n in item.findall(".//CommentsCorrections")]
        authors = [
            " ".join(filter(None, [n.findtext("ForeName"), n.findtext("LastName")]))
            or n.findtext("CollectiveName", "")
            for n in item.findall(".//AuthorList/Author")
        ]
        all_text = " ".join(x["text"] for x in abstract)
        ncts = sorted(
            set(
                re.findall(
                    r"\bNCT\d{8}\b",
                    all_text + " " + " ".join(text(n) for n in item.findall(".//AccessionNumber")),
                )
            )
        )
        snapshot = {
            "pmid": pmid,
            "title": title,
            "abstract": abstract,
            "publication_types": types,
            "authors": authors,
            "journal": text(item.find(".//Journal/Title")),
            "identifiers": ids,
            "publication_date": pub_date(item),
            "comments": comments,
            "xml": ET.tostring(item, encoding="unicode"),
        }
        passages = [{"locator": f"/abstract/{i}/text", "text": a["text"]} for i, a in enumerate(abstract)]
        docs.append(
            SourceDocument(
                source="pubmed",
                canonical_id=pmid,
                url=f"https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/{pmid}/",
                title=title,
                published_date=snapshot["publication_date"],
                retrieved_at=retrieved_at,
                publication_types=types,
                doi=ids.get("doi"),
                nct_ids=ncts,
                journal=snapshot["journal"],
                authors=authors,
                has_results=any(
                    x["label"].lower() in {"results", "findings", "results and conclusions"} for x in abstract
                ),
                retracted="Retracted Publication" in types or "RetractionIn" in comments,
                corrected="ErratumIn" in comments or "UpdateIn" in comments,
                access_level="abstract_only" if abstract else "metadata_only",
                snapshot=snapshot,
                passages=passages,
            )
        )
    return docs


def parse_trial(study: dict, retrieved_at: str) -> SourceDocument:
    protocol = study.get("protocolSection", {})
    identity = protocol.get("identificationModule", {})
    nct = identity.get("nctId", "")
    if not re.fullmatch(r"NCT\d{8}", nct):
        raise SourceFailure("INVALID_NCT_RECORD")
    desc = protocol.get("descriptionModule", {})
    status = protocol.get("statusModule", {})
    design = protocol.get("designModule", {})
    sponsor = protocol.get("sponsorCollaboratorsModule", {})
    passages = []

    def passage(pointer, value):
        if isinstance(value, str) and value.strip():
            passages.append({"locator": pointer, "text": value})

    passage("/protocolSection/identificationModule/briefTitle", identity.get("briefTitle"))
    passage("/protocolSection/descriptionModule/briefSummary", desc.get("briefSummary"))
    passage("/protocolSection/statusModule/overallStatus", status.get("overallStatus"))
    roles = []
    lead = sponsor.get("leadSponsor", {})
    if lead.get("name"):
        pointer = "/protocolSection/sponsorCollaboratorsModule/leadSponsor/name"
        passage(pointer, lead["name"])
        roles.append({"name": lead["name"], "role": "lead_sponsor", "locator": pointer, "study_id": nct})
    for i, collaborator in enumerate(sponsor.get("collaborators", [])):
        if collaborator.get("name"):
            pointer = f"/protocolSection/sponsorCollaboratorsModule/collaborators/{i}/name"
            passage(pointer, collaborator["name"])
            roles.append(
                {"name": collaborator["name"], "role": "collaborator", "locator": pointer, "study_id": nct}
            )
    return SourceDocument(
        source="clinicaltrials",
        canonical_id=nct,
        url=f"https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/{nct}",
        title=identity.get("officialTitle") or identity.get("briefTitle", nct),
        published_date=status.get("studyFirstSubmitDate"),
        updated_date=status.get("lastUpdatePostDateStruct", {}).get("date"),
        retrieved_at=retrieved_at,
        phase=", ".join(design.get("phases", [])) or None,
        status=status.get("overallStatus"),
        has_results=bool(study.get("hasResults") or study.get("resultsSection")),
        nct_ids=[nct],
        access_level="registry_record",
        snapshot=study,
        passages=passages,
        organization_roles=roles,
    )

## 3. Make The Policy Explicit Before Retrieval

Define a versioned source registry with each connector's identity, permitted endpoints/hosts, document classes, allowed claim types, condition coverage, jurisdiction, required metadata and review status. Bind guideline entries to concrete documents/versions. New institutions require a reviewed configuration change; the runtime model cannot add them.

Apply claim-specific boundaries:

- **Current-care claim:** requires an applicable, current guideline passage and attribution to its issuer. Keep historical or uncertain guidance visibly limited.
- **Development claim:** a trial record can establish registered phase/status and intervention details. Preserve missing or non-applicable phase values; do not treat phase as efficacy.
- **Efficacy claim:** requires relevant results in an accessible study report or posted results. Preserve design, population, comparator and endpoint limitations; no-results registration cannot support benefit.
- **Approval claim:** requires the covered regulator's product/indication evidence. Keep regulatory, study and recruitment status separate.
- **Organization claim:** requires a documented role. Sponsor, collaborator, study site, applicant and author affiliation remain distinct; none automatically proves ownership or manufacturing rights.

Use the existing [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-evidence-policy|evidence policy]] for final claim eligibility. Sourcing supplies evidence and metadata-screening results; the downstream validator checks proposed claims against them. A source passing retrieval checks is not a medical truth certification.

## 4. Run The Workflow In A Bounded Sequence

1. **Resolve scope.** Preserve the input and confirm condition/subtype, population and U.S. jurisdiction. Suggest terminology matches; unresolved ambiguity returns clarification. Start with one supported profile.
2. **Build the required source plan.** Code selects the registered guideline, PubMed search, trial search and regulatory path. The model cannot omit required source attempts.
3. **Retrieve baseline evidence.** Fetch guideline/literature/trials independently where possible. Use normalized candidate interventions for targeted FDA lookups afterward. Log queries, filters, timestamps, source failures and result caps.
4. **Capture and normalize.** Retain permitted source text/JSON, stable IDs, source versions/hashes, access level and exact locators. Keep source publication/update dates separate from retrieval time.
5. **Screen metadata and identity.** Check source identity, relevance and applicability; identify missing metadata, retractions/corrections and superseded versions. Domain membership alone is insufficient. Record exclusions and reasons.
6. **Use the agent only for gaps.** It may propose a synonym, intervention alias or narrowly targeted follow-up against the approved tools. The server checks scope, source and remaining budget before execution.
7. **Link and deduplicate.** Connect documents to identifiable NCT/PMID/DOI study families and organization roles. Multiple reports of one study do not become multiple independent studies. Unknown overlap stays unknown.
8. **Return the evidence package.** Include candidate evidence, conflicts, limitations, rejected-item diagnostics and coverage. The application can then validate claims and assemble its briefing.

For the first version, follow only an explicitly approved document link, such as a PubMed record to its registered guideline publisher or permitted PMC article. Use one controlled hop and resolve canonical identifiers directly where available. Do not recursively chase news citations. Record loops or unavailable underlying evidence as unresolved.

Keep U.S. approval/care jurisdiction separate from study geography: ClinicalTrials.gov contains international research. Global studies may inform a U.S. strategy briefing, but their population and applicability must be visible. A recent 30/60-day view is an optional filter for activity, not a restriction on established guidelines. Explain which date each filter uses.

## 5. Separate LLM Access From Search Access

**Provider selected: OpenAI.** Use the Responses API for model access and its hosted `web_search` for supplemental discovery, with registry-derived domain filters and retained source URLs. This capability is documented in [official OpenAI documentation](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search); actual account/model access is untested. Keep the model configurable and `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the backend environment. A separate search vendor is not planned for this route. Direct biomedical connectors remain primary.

The LLM prepares constrained searches and extracts candidate passages. Server tools perform retrieval. An LLM API key enables web search only when the supplied provider/gateway exposes that capability; otherwise a separate search backend is needed. Public biomedical API access is configured independently. The first deterministic retrieval path can work before a model is connected.

Keep the provider adapter and model configurable, with OpenAI selected and no implicit third-party base-URL override. Once credentials are available in backend environment variables, test authentication, a real function-tool round trip, structured output and hosted search on that route. If it lacks a feature, report the limitation and use an explicitly configured alternative; do not silently change providers or describe ordinary API retrieval as model-driven web search.

Start with at most **20 candidate records across the run**, including supplemental retrieval, with provisional slots of one guideline, eight trial records, eight literature records and three regulatory records. Permit at most **two agent follow-up rounds and four supplemental tool calls** within that cap. Apply configured token, cost and wall-time limits, bounded retries and per-source rate controls. Show truncation and unmet coverage. These are engineering defaults to evaluate, not validated medical thresholds or a promise of comprehensive coverage.

## 6. Implement In This Order

| Step | Deliverable | Done when |
|---|---|---|
| 1. Freeze the first profile and policy | U.S. condition profile, source registry, claim-type rules and draft policy version | Required sources and scope are explicit; candidate guideline access is checked |
| 2. Wire ClinicalTrials.gov first | Typed trial records and sponsor/collaborator relationships | One live NCT record and one role can be traced to saved JSON fields; missing/results states remain accurate |
| 3. Add PubMed | Reproducible queries, PMID/DOI records and access labels | One relevant live publication has inspectable metadata and available evidence text |
| 4. Bind the guideline | Versioned, permitted recommendation excerpts | One current-care candidate resolves to the relevant guideline section; otherwise the section is unavailable |
| 5. Add targeted FDA checks | Product/indication lookup with matched/ambiguous/unknown states | One lookup is inspectable and generic labels cannot masquerade as approval proof |
| 6. Add bounded LLM discovery | Provider adapter, constrained search plan and tool execution | A real tool request/result is recorded; the model cannot expand source policy or exceed budgets |
| 7. Package and integrate | Stable sourcing result plus reproducible fixtures | The architecture workstream can consume it without needing scraping logic or provider prompts |

Steps 2–5 produce useful deterministic sourcing. Step 6 adds targeted discovery where gaps justify it. Keep the same output contract for both paths. No full-system framework, database or deployment decision is required to approve this sourcing plan.

## 7. Acceptance And Handoff

The first completed slice must provide an inspectable guideline-supported current-care candidate, a registered emerging-treatment candidate, and a documented organization role, with FDA context or an explicit coverage limitation. Every surfaced evidence ID must resolve to the stored version and exact passage/field. Every source attempt must distinguish success, no matches, blocked access, failure and unattempted work.

Evaluate fixtures for a no-results trial, duplicate study reports, circular citations, superseded/retracted material, different subtypes, incompatible findings, missing organization roles, misleading FDA labels, paywalls, malicious source text, throttling and budget exhaustion. These cases must not become unsupported affirmative care, benefit or approval claims. Preserve conflicting evidence instead of averaging it or taking a model vote. Record reviewer observations separately from automated reference checks.

The integration contract is [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-sourcing-contract|Sourcing runtime contract]]. The broader application receives evidence and coverage; final briefing language and final claim validation remain its responsibility.

**Still required for implementation:** model and credentials supplied through local backend configuration; verification of OpenAI hosted-search access; the first condition/guideline selection and document-access check; operating budget/deadline. OpenAI is selected and U.S. scope is decided. Real domain-policy approval remains a prerequisite for operational use beyond the prototype assumption.

# Healthcare Sourcing Runtime Contract

Proposed v0.1 interface for the [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-sourcing-plan|sourcing plan]]. This is a reviewable contract, not an implemented API or a replacement for the broader application's architecture. Exact adapter field paths must be checked against current source schemas during implementation.

## Input

Expose an internal operation such as `source_condition(scope, policy_version, budget) -> SourcingResult`. The application can wrap it in its chosen API/job system.

| Input | Required meaning |
|---|---|
| `run_id` | Application-supplied correlation ID |
| `scope` | Raw term, confirmed canonical condition/profile ID, subtype/population and jurisdiction `US`; terminology IDs when known |
| `as_of` / `mode` | Requested evidence cutoff; `live` or explicitly labeled `replay` |
| `policy_version` | Installed, fixed source-policy version; runtime arguments cannot redefine its institutions |
| `recent_activity_days` | Optional 30/60-day activity filter; established evidence is retrieved separately |
| `budget` | Server-capped candidate count, tool rounds/calls, token/cost ceiling and deadline |

Do not accept patient records, unrestricted source URLs, prompts that override policy or credentials in research requests. The initial supported profile is proposed adult type 2 diabetes; unknown profiles return a typed unsupported/clarification result.

## Tools And Agent Boundary

| Proposed tool | Server-controlled input | Returns |
|---|---|---|
| `search_trials` | Condition/profile ID; approved condition/intervention terms; bounded filters/count | Normalized trial candidates and source-version IDs |
| `search_pubmed` | Condition/profile ID; bounded terms, publication/date filters/count | Citation/abstract candidates with access labels and IDs |
| `get_guideline` | Registered document ID | Checked version, relevant sections, locators and access limitations |
| `lookup_regulatory_record` | Normalized intervention, exact indication, jurisdiction | Covered matched record, ambiguous or unknown |
| `search_approved_web` | Only if configured: approved source ID, bounded query and purpose | Discovery candidates; content becomes evidence only after retrieval and screening |

Web search is optional for the first slice. A provider-native search tool must support the required restrictions or be replaced by a controlled search adapter. Search snippets are leads, not evidence. Server host checks, approved document paths and redirect checks apply even if the search provider accepts domain filters. The LLM may propose aliases/queries and extract spans; it cannot mutate source policy, choose unregistered authorities, execute arbitrary fetch/shell/filesystem tools or make final eligibility decisions.

## Output Envelope

`SourcingResult` contains:

- `run_id`, `scope`, `mode`, `as_of`, started/finished timestamps and `run_status` (`complete`, `partial`, `needs_clarification`, `unsupported`, `failed`). Complete describes the configured workflow, not an exhaustive medical search.
- `policy_version`, source-registry/parser versions, model/provider and prompt versions when used; no credentials.
- `source_attempts`: source IDs, queries/filters, timings, query cutoff, paging/caps and states `success`, `no_matches`, `blocked`, `failed`, `not_attempted`; retry counts and sanitized reason codes.
- `documents`, `evidence_items`, `organization_roles`, `conflicts`, `limitations`, `screening_decisions` and `coverage` for current care, emerging treatments, organizations and regulatory context.
- `usage`: tool calls, rounds, tokens and measured cost when available. Unknown price/usage stays unknown. `stop_reason` distinguishes deadline, provider/source failure, completed plan and budget exhaustion.

Coverage is `covered`, `limited` or `unavailable`, with supporting evidence IDs and reasons. Reaching a record cap makes relevant coverage limited. No-match, inaccessible evidence and connector failure remain distinct. Cached/replay evidence retains its original retrieval time and is never presented as a new live search.

## Evidence And Relationship Records

| Record | Minimum fields |
|---|---|
| Source document/version | Stable connector and canonical ID/URL, original publisher/issuer, document class, version/hash/snapshot reference, publication/update/retrieval dates, access level and parser version |
| Evidence item | Evidence ID, source-version ID, excerpt or structured field value, exact page/section/JSON-pointer locator, scope/applicability, permitted claim types, known limitations and correction/retraction/supersession state |
| Study metadata | NCT/PMID/DOI links when known, design, population, phase/status, results availability and endpoint context where available; separate regulatory match |
| Evidence family | Underlying study identifier and documented links between reports; unknown membership/overlap remains explicit |
| Organization role | Recorded organization name, normalized ID if supported, role type, study/intervention link, source-version ID and locator; dates when available |
| Screening decision | Candidate ID, policy version, `pass`, `limited` or `exclude`, reason codes and review-needed flag; this is metadata screening, not final claim validation |
| Conflict | Linked evidence IDs, potential disagreement, differences in scope/date/endpoint and review-needed flag |

Content must be accessible and permitted to retain. Do not fabricate a full-text snapshot for an abstract-only article. Check proposed quotations/values against their saved versions. A correct quote still needs semantic and applicability review before becoming a final claim. Preserve missing data as null/unknown rather than filling it from model memory.

## Source Registry And Credentials

The registry records source identity, allowed endpoints/hosts and redirects, document types, claim-type permissions, jurisdiction/condition coverage, required fields, access method and review status. A guideline entry binds issuer, document/version and relevant sections. Every result records the registry version used; refreshes create new source versions.

The owner selects OpenAI. The new backend repository provides an ignored `.env` with blank `OPENAI_API_KEY`, `NCBI_API_KEY`, `OPENAI_MODEL` and optional `NCBI_EMAIL`. Use OpenAI's default endpoint and make the model configurable. These actual setup names replace the earlier proposed `LLM_MODEL` convention; the architecture may map them through its settings layer. Avoid implicit third-party base-URL overrides. Keep keys in backend environment variables or the ignored secret file; ignore rules and untracked status are verified. No environment loader exists yet. Credentials, model choice and account capabilities remain untested; no silent provider fallback.

Map supplemental web discovery to Responses API hosted `web_search` with registry-derived domain filters; retain consulted-source URLs and citation annotations. Recheck candidates before admission. Keep this hosted tool distinct from application-executed biomedical function tools, which use strict schemas and local argument validation. Measure hosted search usage separately and enforce request/tool/token/deadline budgets in the adapter. No separate search-vendor credential is planned for this route; biomedical API configuration remains independent. See [OpenAI web search](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/tools-web-search) and [function calling](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling).

## Failure And Consumer Responsibilities

Timeout/429/transient failures use bounded retries and source-specific limits; blocked access is not bypassed. Budget stops return the available evidence with gaps. Treat source text as untrusted data and ignore embedded instructions. Return sanitized errors and keep secret headers out of logs.

The consuming application validates claim support under the [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-evidence-policy|evidence policy]], retains opposing evidence, and displays access/coverage limitations. It must not promote a metadata-screening pass into an approval, efficacy or standard-care claim. The sourcing component supplies provenance and candidates; final synthesis, human review, presentation and deployment remain with their respective workstreams.

The American Diabetes Association (ADA) “Standards of Care in Diabetes” includes the ADA’s current clinical practice recommendations and is intended to provide the components of diabetes care, general treatment goals and guidelines, and tools to evaluate quality of care. Members of the ADA Link to Introduction and Methodology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026Professional Practice Committee for Diabetes, an interprofessional expert committee, are responsible for updating the Standards of Care annually, or more frequently as warranted. For a detailed description of ADA standards, statements, and reports, as well as the evidence-grading system for ADA’s clinical practice recommendations and a full list of Professional Practice Committee members, please refer to Link to Introduction and Methodology: Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026Introduction and Methodology. Readers who wish to comment on the Standards of Care are invited to do so at Link to Standards of Care in Diabetesprofessional.diabetes.org/SOC.

## Systems to Support Diabetes Population Health

#### Recommendations

  * 1.1 Ensure treatment decisions are timely, rely on evidence-based guidelines, address social determinants of health, and incorporate shared decision-making based on individual values, preferences, prognoses, comorbidities, and informed financial considerations. B

  * 1.2 Align approaches to diabetes management with evidence-based care models. These models emphasize person-centered team care, integrated long-term treatment approaches to diabetes and comorbidities, and ongoing collaborative communication and goal setting among all team members and with people with diabetes. A

  * 1.3 Care systems should facilitate in-person and virtual team-based care, include those knowledgeable and experienced in diabetes management as part of the team, and utilize patient registries, decision support tools, proactive care planning, and community involvement to meet needs of individuals with diabetes. ## Summary

Improving individual and population health for people with and at risk for diabetes requires engagement of and collaboration between people with diabetes and their caregivers, interprofessional health care teams, health systems, community partners, payors, policymakers, and public health agencies. This section provides guidance to facilitate implementation of evidence-based diabetes care recommendations that are discussed in the Standards of Care with the goal of improving health, eliminating health disparities, and reducing the impact of diabetes and its complications on individuals and society.

name: llm-wiki-ingest
description: Compile a Raw source into concise, linked Wiki notes. Use when a new source lands in Raw/Sources/ or when a source is marked Processed:false.
---

# LLM Wiki Ingest

Turn a Raw source into short, reusable, source-linked Wiki notes.

## Steps

1. Confirm the source file lives in `Raw/Sources/` and has valid source
   frontmatter (`Title`, `Reference`, `Created`, `Processed`, `tags: [source]`).
2. Search the catalog before opening anything broad:

   ```bash
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py search-catalog --query "<source topic>"
   ```

3. Open only the most relevant existing Wiki notes. Prefer updating an
   existing note over creating a near-duplicate.
4. Read the Raw source and extract its distinct, reusable claims.
5. Create or update focused notes under `Wiki/` using the templates in
   `_templates/`. One idea per note. Use the correct folder and tag
   (see `Schema/naming-conventions.md`).
6. In every note you create or touch, add the Raw source path to `sources`
   and keep `source_count` equal to `len(sources)`. Bump `updated`.
7. Rebuild and validate:

   ```bash
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py build
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py lint
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-scan --update --accept-covered
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-lint
   ```

8. If the ingest meaningfully changed the Wiki, add a log entry:

   ```bash
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py log --title "Ingested <source>" --details "<what changed>"
   ```

## Rules

- Never invent claims the source does not support.
- Never edit the Raw source content itself (frontmatter `Processed` is
  managed by `source-scan --update --accept-covered`).
- Keep the transformation visible: a small source becomes a few focused notes,
  not one giant dump.
---
name: llm-wiki-maintain
description: Routine maintenance and safe commits. Use when committing changes, rebuilding indexes, or checking overall vault health.
---

# LLM Wiki Maintain

Keep the vault healthy and every commit clean.

## Maintenance Gate (before every meaningful commit)

```bash
python scripts/wiki_tool.py doctor
python scripts/wiki_tool.py build
python scripts/wiki_tool.py lint
python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-lint
python scripts/audit_public.py
```

After source ingestion, also run:

```bash
python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-scan --update --accept-covered
python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-lint
```

All commands must pass before committing.

## Routine Tasks

- **Coverage review:** `python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-coverage` shows
  which Raw sources are covered by Wiki notes; `source-delta` shows sources
  missing from the manifest.
- **Index rebuild:** `build` regenerates `Wiki/catalog.jsonl`, `Wiki/index.md`,
  and per-folder indexes. Commit the regenerated artifacts.
- **Logging:** record meaningful changes with
  `python scripts/wiki_tool.py log --title "..." --details "..."`.
- **Hooks:** `scripts/install_hooks.sh` points git at `.githooks/` so the
  pre-commit hook runs the full gate (doctor, build, lint, source-lint,
  audit_public) automatically.

## Rules

- Never commit with failing checks.
- Never commit secrets, machine-local paths, or plugin/cache state —
  `scripts/audit_public.py` guards this; take its failures seriously.
- Keep commits scoped: content changes and generated artifacts may share a
  commit, but unrelated changes should not.
# The Relay Protocol — Claude Code ⇄ Codex with zero copy-paste

Two different coding agents work this project. They never share a chat window,
but they share three things that live in this repo:

1. **The baton** — [`STATE.md`](STATE.md): a short, always-current statement of
   where the work stands. The ONLY file an agent must read to pick up the work.
2. **The history** — [`HISTORY.md`](HISTORY.md): stamped, newest-first handoff
   entries (who, when, at which commit, what happened).
3. **Git** — every handoff sits on a commit, so "what changed" is always
   diffable and nothing depends on anyone's chat scrollback.

Everything else (the Wiki, the code graphs, the chat archive) is shared memory
both agents already read the same way. The relay is only the *baton pass*.

## The two moves

### CATCH UP (start of any session, either agent)

1. Read `_relay/STATE.md` top to bottom.
2. Run `python scripts/relay_tool.py status` — it warns if commits landed
   *after* the last handoff (a stale baton).
3. Run `git log --oneline -10` for the recent trail.
4. If more depth is needed: newest `Wiki/Logs/` note → project note's Status +
   Next Steps. Do **not** re-read raw sources or sweep the codebase to resume.
5. Say back, in a few sentences, where things stand and what you'll do next.
   Then work.

### HAND OFF (end of any session that changed anything)

1. Edit `_relay/STATE.md` — rewrite the sections (they describe the PRESENT,
   not a diff): `Now`, `Just landed`, `Next`, `Open questions`, `Watch out`.
   Write for the *other* agent: no chat references ("as discussed above"),
   no session-local shorthand, absolute honesty about what is unfinished.
2. Stamp it:
   `python scripts/relay_tool.py stamp --agent <claude|codex> --summary "<one paragraph>"`
3. Run the maintenance gate (see `AGENTS.md`), then **commit** — the baton
   travels with the commit.

## Rules

- **The baton describes state, not effort.** "Auth middleware works, tests
  green, refresh-token path untested" beats a play-by-play of the session.
- **Never hand off a lie.** If the gate fails or tests are red, STATE.md says
  so in `Watch out`.
- **One baton.** Agents don't keep private TODO files; anything worth
  remembering goes in STATE.md (short-term) or the Wiki (long-term).
- **Stale baton = read git first.** If `relay_tool.py status` warns, trust
  `git log` + the newest `Wiki/Logs/` note over STATE.md, then fix STATE.md.
- **Session transcripts are local memory.** `python scripts/import_chats.py`
  archives both agents' transcripts (Claude Code *and* Codex) into `chats/`
  — gitignored, searchable, never committed.

## Why this works for both agents

- **Claude Code** loads `CLAUDE.md`, which wires `catchup` / `save` / `handoff`
  to this protocol (plus `/catchup`, `/save`, `/handoff` commands).
- **Codex** loads `AGENTS.md`, which states the same two moves as hard rules.
- Both write the same file with the same stamp tool, so neither cares which
  agent came before.

## The two modes

| Mode | What | Where |
|---|---|---|
| **Async — the baton** (this file's protocol) | agents alternate across sessions; state travels via STATE.md + git | `_relay/STATE.md`, `_relay/HISTORY.md` |
| **Sync — sparring** | both models in one session: the driver plans/builds, the rival attacks the plan (read-only rounds) and grades the diff | `_relay/spar/` — `PLAN.md`, `SPAR-LOG.md`, machine-local `state.json`, finished spars in `archive/`; driven by `scripts/spar_tool.py` + the `sparring` skill |

A spar in flight is baton-visible: STATE.md's **Now**/**Watch out** name it,
and `python scripts/spar_tool.py status` lets any session resume the loop.

"""Explicit condition/population scope. Titles and eligibility have different roles."""

import re


class ScopeAmbiguity(ValueError):
    pass


def normalized(value: str) -> str:
    return " ".join(re.findall(r"[a-z0-9]+", value.lower()))


def diabetes_type(value: str) -> str | None:
    value = normalized(value)
    if re.search(r"\b(?:gestational diabetes|gdm)\b", value):
        return "gestational_diabetes"
    if re.search(r"\b(?:type (?:2|ii) diabetes|diabetes (?:mellitus )?type (?:2|ii)|t2dm|t2d)\b", value):
        return "type_2_diabetes"
    if re.search(r"\b(?:type (?:1|i) diabetes|diabetes (?:mellitus )?type (?:1|i)|t1dm|t1d)\b", value):
        return "type_1_diabetes"
    return None


def population_tags(value: str) -> list[str]:
    """Only positive population wording; tissue provenance is never a population."""
    patterns = {
        "pregnancy": r"\b(?:pregnan\w*|gestational|maternal)\b",
        "pediatric": r"\b(?:children|childhood|pediatric|paediatric|adolescen\w*|youth)\b",
        "obesity": r"\b(?:obesity|obese|overweight)\b",
        "kidney_disease": r"\b(?:chronic kidney disease|ckd|renal impairment|dialysis)\b",
        "cardiovascular_disease": r"\b(?:heart failure|cardiovascular disease|atherosclerotic)\b",
    }
    return [key for key, pattern in patterns.items() if re.search(pattern, value, re.I)]


def resolve_scope(condition: str, population: str = "general", *, allow_ambiguous=False) -> dict:
    key = diabetes_type(condition)
    if not key and re.search(r"\bdiabet(?:es|ic)\b", condition, re.I) and not allow_ambiguous:
        raise ScopeAmbiguity(
            "Specify type 1, type 2, or gestational diabetes before researching this condition."
        )
    labels = {
        "type_2_diabetes": "Type 2 diabetes",
        "type_1_diabetes": "Type 1 diabetes",
        "gestational_diabetes": "Gestational diabetes",
    }
    requested = population_tags(condition)
    if population != "general" and population not in requested:
        requested.append(population)
    return {
        "raw_condition": condition,
        "condition": labels.get(key, condition),
        "condition_key": key or normalized(condition),
        "population": requested or ["general"],
        "jurisdiction": "US",
    }


def condition_matches(scope: dict, title: str, conditions: list[str], body: str) -> bool:
    # Structured registry conditions win over mentions in background or exclusions.
    corpus = " ".join(conditions) if conditions else title + " " + body
    if scope["condition_key"] in {"type_1_diabetes", "type_2_diabetes", "gestational_diabetes"}:
        if not conditions and diabetes_type(title):
            return diabetes_type(title) == scope["condition_key"]
        return diabetes_type(corpus) == scope["condition_key"]
    words = set(normalized(scope["condition"]).split()) - {"of", "the", "and", "in"}
    return bool(words) and words <= set(normalized(corpus).split())


def trial_population(protocol: dict) -> dict:
    identity = protocol.get("identificationModule", {})
    conditions = protocol.get("conditionsModule", {}).get("conditions", [])
    eligibility = protocol.get("eligibilityModule", {})
    criteria = eligibility.get("eligibilityCriteria", "")
    inclusion = re.split(r"exclusion criteria\s*:", criteria, maxsplit=1, flags=re.I)[0]
    # Ignore negative lines, including common pregnancy exclusion/contraception language.
    positive_lines = [
        line
        for line in inclusion.splitlines()
        if not re.search(r"\b(?:not|non|no|exclude\w*|negative|contracept\w*)\b", line, re.I)
    ]
    population_text = " ".join(
        [identity.get("officialTitle", ""), identity.get("briefTitle", ""), *conditions, *positive_lines]
    )
    tags = population_tags(population_text)
    ages = eligibility.get("stdAges", [])
    if ages == ["CHILD"] and "pediatric" not in tags:
        tags.append("pediatric")
    return {
        "conditions": conditions,
        "tags": tags,
        "minimum_age": eligibility.get("minimumAge"),
        "maximum_age": eligibility.get("maximumAge"),
        "sex": eligibility.get("sex"),
        "eligibility_criteria": criteria,
        "countries": sorted(
            {
                x["country"]
                for x in protocol.get("contactsLocationsModule", {}).get("locations", [])
                if x.get("country")
            }
        ),
    }
"}

+    study["protocolSection"]["identificationModule"]["briefTitle"] = "Type 2 diabetes in pregnant adults"

+    assert all(validate_claim(x, [c])[0] for x in claims)

+def test_observational_study_cannot_be_an_emerging_treatment_even_if_recent_and_active():

+        assert citation(active_study(), condition)["decision"] != "excluded"

+"""Read-only policy replay of stored source versions; no discovery/model calls or report mutation.
+
+Run from backend: python -m scripts.trace_citation --run-id <id> --nct-id NCT01954147
+"""
+
+import argparse
+from datetime import date
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from sqlalchemy import select
+from app.database import Session, ResearchRun, Citation, SourceSnapshot
+from app.schemas import SourceDocument
+from app.sources import parse_trial
+from app.policy import rank_documents, validate_claim, POLICY_VERSION
+from app.workflow import structured_claims
+
+
+def trace(run_id, nct_id):
+    with Session() as db:
+        run = db.get(ResearchRun, run_id)
+        if not run or not run.result:
+            raise ValueError("Saved completed run required")
+        before = run.result
+        rows = list(db.scalars(select(Citation).where(Citation.run_id == run_id)))
+        documents = []
+        for row in rows:
+            snapshot = db.get(SourceSnapshot, row.snapshot_id).data
+            if row.data["source"] == "clinicaltrials":
+                documents.append(parse_trial(snapshot, row.data["retrieved_at"]))
+            else:
+                fields = {k: v for k, v in row.data.items() if k in SourceDocument.model_fields}
+                documents.append(SourceDocument(**fields, snapshot=snapshot,
+                                               passages=[{"locator": e["locator"], "text": e["text"]}
+                                                         for e in row.data["evidence"]]))
+        after = rank_documents(documents, run.condition, run_id, run.request.get("population", "general"),
+                               as_of=date.fromisoformat(before["as_of"][:10]))
+        accepted = structured_claims(after)
+        withheld = []
+        # Revalidate the original model claims against the same immutable source versions.
+        for claim in before["claims"]:
+            if claim["origin"] == "structured_source_fields":
+                continue
+            ok, reasons, _ = validate_claim(claim, after)
+            (accepted if ok else withheld).append(claim if ok else {"text": claim["text"], "reason_codes": reasons})
+        old = next(c for c in before["citations"] if c["canonical_id"] == nct_id)
+        new = next(c for c in after if c["canonical_id"] == nct_id)
+        old_claims = [c for c in before["claims"] if any(r["citation_id"] == old["id"] for r in c["references"])]
+        new_claims = [c for c in accepted if any(r["evidence_id"] in {e["id"] for e in new["evidence"]}
+                                                for r in c["references"])]
+        return {
+            "mode": "saved_snapshot_policy_replay", "original_run_id": run_id, "request": run.request,
+            "source_attempts": before["source_attempts"], "source_as_of": before["as_of"],
+            "original_policy": before["policy_version"], "replay_policy": POLICY_VERSION,
+            "new_source_or_model_calls": 0, "original_results_modified": False,
+            "target": {"canonical_id": nct_id, "snapshot_hash": old["snapshot_hash"],
+                       "before": old, "after": {k: v for k, v in new.items() if k != "snapshot"},
+                       "before_claims": old_claims, "after_claims": new_claims,
+                       "selected_by_original_model": any(old["id"] in t.get("citation_ids", [])
+                                                         for t in before["usage"]["tool_calls"])},
+            "before_claim_count": len(before["claims"]), "after_claim_count": len(accepted),
+            "replay_claims": accepted, "withheld_original_model_claims": withheld,
+            "limitation": "This isolates changed parser/policy behavior on the original saved sources. It revalidates original model text; it is not a new live search or a new semantic review.",
+        }
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--run-id", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--nct-id", default="NCT01954147")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    result = trace(args.run_id, args.nct_id)
+    output = Path("data") / f"trace-{args.nct_id.lower()}.json"
+    output.parent.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
+    output.write_text(json.dumps(result, indent=2), encoding="utf-8")
+    print(json.dumps({"output": str(output), "policy": result["replay_policy"],
+                      "before_claims_for_target": len(result["target"]["before_claims"]),
+                      "after_claims_for_target": len(result["target"]["after_claims"]),
+                      "reasons": result["target"]["after"]["reason_codes"],
+                      "population": result["target"]["after"]["population"]}, indent=2))
*** End Patch"));

Evidence Desk is implemented and running locally: React/TypeScript UI, FastAPI API and PostgreSQL in Docker Compose. # Healthcare Evidence Runtime

> [!info] Baseline and concurrent correction
> Backend `5e62673` and frontend `862f36f` save the implemented application. The baseline test command passes 31 tests including early shared scope checks; the v2 live result below is historical evidence. The separate active chat **Trace trial result mismatch** is continuing policy-v3 condition/population and trial-currency corrections. Its uncommitted edits are preserved; verify its later handoff before claiming the newest policy is fully deployed or tested. See the handoff source for the boundary.

The implemented layer after sourcing authenticates source identity, ranks citations under fixed policy, links claims to saved passages, and preserves potential conflicting findings. It is available through the local Evidence Desk application at [localhost:5173](http://localhost:5173), with API documentation at [localhost:8000/docs](http://localhost:8000/docs).

## Implemented Flow

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    S[Canonical PMID/NCT identifiers] --> F[Fixed API re-fetch]
    F --> V[Source identity and snapshot checks]
    V --> P[Deterministic admission and ordering]
    P --> L[Bounded evidence tool and extraction]
    L --> C[Quote and semantic support checks]
    C --> D[Potential conflict links]
    D --> R[Cited briefing and exports]
    V --> DB[(PostgreSQL snapshots and passages)]
    C --> DB
    D --> DB
```

`backend/app/policy.py` owns policy version `us-evidence-2026-10-27.v2`. Ordering uses source admission, condition match, evidence class, results, dates and stable IDs. It does not score clinical truth or patient suitability. Retractions and identity mismatches are excluded; limitations remain explicit.

`backend/app/workflow.py` connects claims to evidence IDs and quotations. `backend/app/database.py` stores runs, immutable snapshots, citations, passages, claims, claim-evidence links, conflicts and events in PostgreSQL. Source text is untrusted data. No model can modify source authority, execute arbitrary fetches or bypass a failed gate.

## Integration Contract

The implemented upstream seam is `POST /api/evidence/process`, returning 202 and a run ID. Required fields include a condition and `scope_confirmed: true`; optional source lists are `pmids` and `nct_ids`, with US/live scope. At least one identifier is required. The service re-fetches IDs rather than trusting caller-provided text or verification flags. `POST /api/research-runs` adds its own bounded PubMed/trial discovery before the same pipeline.

Poll `GET /api/research-runs/{id}`. Inspect `GET /api/citations/{id}` and `/snapshot`. Export `/api/research-runs/{id}/export?format=markdown|json`. The report retains its run policy version, dates, scope, gaps, original evidence references and content hashes. Keys remain in the ignored backend environment; the optional application token is separate.

## Conflicting Citations

Accepted claims with explicit matching intervention/population/outcome and opposing findings create a potential conflict. Both claims and citations remain visible and unresolved. An analyst compares study design, comparator, dates and applicability. The system does not average contradictory findings or use model votes to choose a winner. Exact matching can miss differently worded conflicts, so no detected conflict is not consensus.

## Verified Local Slice

The policy-v2 type 2 diabetes example retrieves eight records, stores ten accepted/structured claims, and withholds three candidates. The model makes one actual allowlisted evidence-tool call across three requests. Twenty backend tests pass using actual PostgreSQL; production frontend/Docker builds and desktop/mobile browser checks pass. These are implementation observations, not clinical validation. See the source implementation record for the specific run ID and check details.

Run from the backend repository with `docker compose up -d --build`. Compose runs API, frontend and PostgreSQL locally; database data persists in a named volume. Backend tests: `uv run pytest -q`; actual running-service smoke: `uv run python scripts/smoke_http.py`.

## Remaining Boundaries

No checked current US guideline or FDA connector is wired. Current standard of care and approval claims are withheld, rather than inferred from PubMed indexing or registry presence. PubMed abstracts do not establish full-paper review. Automated semantic checking is probabilistic and expert appraisal remains necessary. Prototype jobs are single-process and become interrupted on restart; production identity/tenants, durable workers and migrations are future pilot work.

See [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-evidence-policy|Evidence policy]], [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-sourcing-contract|Sourcing contract]], [[Wiki/Concepts/healthcare-data-and-provenance|Provenance design]], and [[Wiki/Projects/healthcare-system|Project hub]].

"""Run the actual Docker/API workflow using the configured backend keys; print sanitized evidence counts."""

import json, time
from pathlib import Path
import httpx
from app.config import get_settings

settings = get_settings()
token = settings.app_access_token.get_secret_value()
headers = {"Authorization": "Bearer " + token} if token else {}
with httpx.Client(base_url="http://localhost:8000", headers=headers, timeout=10) as client:
    response = client.post(
        "/api/research-runs",
        json={
            "condition": "Type 2 diabetes",
            "scope_confirmed": True,
            "mode": "live",
            "use_llm": True,

        },
    )
    response.raise_for_status()
    run_id = response.json()["id"]
    print("Started live API run " + run_id, flush=True)
    deadline = time.monotonic() + 170
    while time.monotonic() < deadline:
        response = client.get("/api/research-runs/" + run_id)
        response.raise_for_status()
        run = response.json()
        if run["status"] not in {"queued", "running"}:

    result = run.get("result")

text(await tools.apply_patch("*** Begin Patch
*** Add File: [PROJECT_ROOT]/omnia-vault/Raw/Sources/2026-10-27-evidence-scope-trace.md
+---
+Title: "Owner-requested trace and correction of the diabetes briefing mismatch"
+Reference: "Owner request, attached Evidence Desk screenshot, saved PostgreSQL source versions, local code and verification, 2026-10-27"
+ContentType:
+  - "markdown"
+Created: 2026-10-27
+Processed: false
+tags:
+  - "source"
+---
+
+# Request And Observed Evidence
+
+The owner supplied ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT01954147 and an Evidence Desk screenshot, asking to trace how the result reached the briefing, identify whether search, retrieval, extraction or synthesis caused the mismatch, correct the pipeline, distinguish general conditions from specific populations, and rerun the same condition. The accompanying conversation described pregnancy-specific evidence for a type 2 diabetes input, a standard-care gap, and emerging-treatment/company relevance. The conversation is evidence of the requested behavior, not an instruction to trust its clinical interpretation.
+
+## Original Run
+
+- Run: `d9e18095-7c51-4688-9e2f-96d682c52f98`, policy v1, condition `Type 2 diabetes`, US, eight-record cap, live mode, model enabled. Four PubMed and four trial records were saved.
+- Target citation: `cit_5816b118ee11720571114886`, rank 5, 3/3 condition words matched, trial status `UNKNOWN`, last update posted `2014-02-20`, no posted registry results. Snapshot SHA-256: `58913d03511e3b77a42090f38486317e36d2e3828d444aeb5948fc44449387a0`.
+- Actual trial eligibility: type 2 diabetes, men and women aged 35–65, China. Positive pregnancy test and breastfeeding are exclusions. Umbilical cord describes the cell source; this is not a pregnancy cohort. The source also links a publication, so absence of posted registry results must not be described as absence of all published research.
+- Original source: [ClinicalTrials.gov record](https://clinicaltrials.gov/study/NCT01954147); structured source: [official API record](https://clinicaltrials.gov/api/v2/studies/NCT01954147).
+- Actual pregnancy-specific paper: [PMID 39084811](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/39084811/), “Diagnosis and Treatment of Hyperglycemia in Pregnancy: Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus and Gestational Diabetes.” Pediatric paper: [PMID 27974926](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/27974926/). Their findings appeared under general published care evidence. A cognitive-impairment paper also needed a separate population label.
+
+## Causal Trace
+
+1. The request confirmed a condition and US scope but did not resolve a separate population.
+2. The saved PubMed query was `"Type 2 diabetes"[Title/Abstract] AND humans[MeSH Terms]`. The saved trial attempt recorded the condition, four-record cap and retrieval date, without a complete raw HTTP parameter log. Initially inspected connector code had no trial currency/status filter. Do not invent the original upstream order beyond the recorded rank/cap.
+3. `parse_trial` retained full source JSON but exposed only title, summary, registry status and sponsor/collaborator passages to downstream processing. Eligibility, conditions, interventions, age and geography were not exposed as structured screening inputs.
+4. `rank_documents` admitted sources based on identity, retraction and word overlap. Three condition-word matches sufficed for ordering; population, unknown recruitment status and the 2014 update did not gate emerging activity.
+5. `structured_claims` copied every admitted registry title into emerging treatments and every sponsor into organizations. It recorded population as unknown and bypassed model semantic review as a field copy. This target produced one development statement and one sponsor statement.
+6. The stored model tool-call IDs contain only the four PubMed citations, not the target trial. The two target claims therefore did not originate from model extraction. The model did preserve pregnancy/childhood wording in the literature statements, but synthesis displayed them under the general section because no population lane was enforced.
+7. Current-care coverage was set to unavailable for every run because no registered guideline connector exists. The UI's “not established” headline conflated missing system coverage with the state of clinical care. The source date also displayed a day early because a date-only UTC value was formatted in US local time.
+
+## Implemented Correction
+
+Policy `us-evidence-2026-10-27.v3` resolves diabetes subtype aliases, rejects ambiguous live `diabetes` input with a clarification, and retains raw/canonical condition plus population in the run and query attempts. Trial parsing exposes eligibility, positive inclusion criteria, conditions, ages, sex, countries, interventions and organization class. Pregnancy exclusions, including parenthesized exclusion headings, and cord tissue do not become pregnancy inclusion labels.
+

+| Standard care | Hard-coded unavailable coverage headed “not established” | State that guideline retrieval is missing; do not imply the condition has no established care |
+| Display | Date-only UTC parsing shifted February 20 to February 19 | Preserve date precision in US local display; mark saved reports using older policies |

# AGENTS.md — Omnia Vault Rules

This folder is an **Omnia Vault**: an Obsidian **LLM Wiki** (captured sources
compiled into short, linked, source-traceable notes) + **Graphify code graphs**
of any tracked repos + a **relay** that lets different coding agents (Codex,
Claude Code, …) work the same project with zero copy-paste. The vault is the
project's memory; your chat history is not.

Every agent working in this folder follows these rules. The narrative guide is
[VAULT-GUIDE.md](VAULT-GUIDE.md); Claude-specific wiring is in
[CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md).

## The relay — FIRST and LAST thing in every session

- **Session start:** read `_relay/STATE.md` (the baton), run
  `python scripts/relay_tool.py status` and `git log --oneline -10`, then tell
  the user where things stand. Do not re-read raw sources or sweep code to
  resume. If the status tool warns the baton is stale, trust git + the newest
  `Wiki/Logs/` note, then repair STATE.md.
- **Session end (or when the user switches agents):** rewrite
  `_relay/STATE.md` (sections: Now / Just landed / Next / Open questions /
  Watch out — present-tense state, written for a stranger, brutally honest
  about what's unfinished), stamp it with
  `python scripts/relay_tool.py stamp --agent codex --summary "<paragraph>"`
  (use your own agent name), run the maintenance gate, and **commit**.
- Full protocol: `_relay/PROTOCOL.md`.

## Layers

| Layer | Path | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|
| Raw sources | `Raw/Sources/` | Captured source material (transcripts, articles, notes). Never treat as compiled knowledge. |
| Raw files | `Raw/Files/` | Binary/attachment sources. Gitignored except `.gitkeep`. |
| Compiled Wiki | `Wiki/` | Short, linked, reusable notes compiled from Raw sources. The product. |
| Code graphs | `graphify/<repo>/` | Committed Graphify snapshots of tracked repos (generated — never hand-edit). |
| Relay | `_relay/` | The agent-to-agent baton (STATE.md), history, protocol. |
| Schema | `Schema/` | Frontmatter contracts, naming, lint rules, command reference. |
| Templates | `_templates/` | Note templates for every note type. |
| Tooling | `scripts/` | Deterministic build/lint/audit/relay tools (python stdlib only). |
| Chat archive | `chats/` | Both agents' transcripts as **local memory** (gitignored; secrets redacted on import). |

## Core rules

1. **Write reusable knowledge only under `Wiki/`** — topics in `Wiki/Topics/`,
   concepts in `Wiki/Concepts/`, entities in `Wiki/Entities/`, projects in
   `Wiki/Projects/`, logs in `Wiki/Logs/`.
2. **Never edit Raw sources to "improve" them**; compile them into `Wiki/`
   notes instead.
3. **Every compiled note links to its Raw sources**: `sources` lists real
   files under `Raw/Sources/`, and `source_count == len(sources)`. Never
   invent citations — no source, no claim (capture it as an Open Question).
4. **Search before reading broadly:**
   `python scripts/wiki_tool.py search-catalog --query "text"` first; open Raw
   sources only when compiled notes are insufficient. For code questions, the
   graph comes even earlier — see the 3-Layer Query Rule below.
5. **Maintenance gate before every commit** (use `python3` on macOS/Linux):

   ```bash
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py doctor
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py build
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py lint
   python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-lint
   python scripts/audit_public.py
   ```

   After source ingestion, also
   `python scripts/wiki_tool.py source-scan --update --accept-covered` then
   `source-lint`. All must pass.
6. **Never commit:** secrets, machine-local absolute paths, tracked work-repo
   code (gitignore repo folders; only `graphify/<repo>/` snapshots are
   committed), Obsidian plugin/cache state, or hand edits to generated files
   (`Wiki/catalog.jsonl`, `*/index.md`, `Schema/source-manifest.jsonl`,
   `graphify/`).

## 3-Layer Query Rule (questions about the project/code)

1. **Graph:** `graphify query "<question>" --graph graphify/<repo>/graph.json`
   (also `explain` / `path` / `affected`; overview in
   `graphify/<repo>/_GRAPH_REPORT.md` and `_COMMUNITY_*.md`).
2. **Wiki:** `python scripts/wiki_tool.py search-catalog --query "<topic>"` →
   top 1–3 notes.
3. **Raw:** the cited source file / the specific code files only.

## Workflows (readable by any agent — follow the file, not the folder name)

- Ingest a source: `.claude/skills/llm-wiki-ingest/SKILL.md`

- Cross-model decision panel (breadth, before locking a direction):
